page: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs, derived from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via an 885 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2904.58 and a PassMark memory score of 2848.4, both placing in the top 25 percent. Image processing performance is also strong, scoring 14481.0 on Geekbench. Multi-core performance metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 43303.38 and Geekbench multi-core score of 14309.0, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 77.97 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 44.59 GB/sec for large-block write operations. For language model workloads, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 274.92 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, but performance drops to a weak 6.62 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a large 70B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-32as_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the need to scale up to higher vCPU tiers. The inclusion of an 885 GB local SSD provides fast temporary storage, reducing dependency on external network-attached storage for caching. This hardware configuration is well-suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EASv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs, 512.0 GB of RAM, and an 885 GB local SSD. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong single-core CPU and memory performance, as evidenced by its top-tier PassMark memory score and stress-ng single-core results. While multi-core processing and memory bandwidth remain average, its high memory density makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads. However, it exhibits weak performance on large-scale LLM inference tasks. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, including large databases, in-memory caches, and data processing pipelines.
